title: Eastgrove Power how to read your bill
brief: Eastgrove Power wants a plain-language page explaining how to read a residential electricity bill, written for customers by the Customer Education team, for rates effective 2026-11-01. Headings: "Your bill at a glance", "What each charge means", "Time-of-use hours", "Ways to lower your bill". The facts: a bill has a fixed monthly service charge of 14.50 dollars, a delivery charge of 0.045 dollars per kilowatt-hour (kWh) and a supply charge that depends on when you use power; supply costs 0.31 dollars per kWh at peak, 0.12 off-peak and 0.08 super off-peak; peak is 16:00 to 21:00 on weekdays, super off-peak is 00:00 to 06:00 every day, and everything else is off-peak; sales tax of 5.2 percent applies to the total; the bill is due 21 days after the bill date, and a late payment fee of 1.5 percent is added to unpaid balances after that; budget billing spreads the year into 12 equal payments reviewed every 6 months; income-qualified households can get a 20 percent discount through the CARE program, and enrolling takes about 10 minutes online. Ways to lower the bill: run the dishwasher and laundry after 21:00, precool the house before 16:00 and set the thermostat 2 degrees higher during peak, and charge electric vehicles after midnight. Explain that peak power costs more than 2.5 times as much as off-peak power. Customers can call 800-555-0166 or use the online account page.

edit.request: Change the peak supply rate to 0.34 dollars per kWh, the peak window to 17:00 to 21:00, and the late payment fee to 2 percent.
